header: Date: 2026-11-30 / Time: 10:00 PT / Duration: ~62 minutes / Attendees: Redwood AE+SE, Ember Medical InfoSec + CTO + Platform
summary: Discovery focused on Ember Medical's security posture and whether Redwood Hosted or Dedicated/Private deployment meets their compliance and encryption requirements. Key topics: SOC 2, ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS (BYOK), data residency and retention. Action: send SOC2 report, schedule DEEP technical benchmark, share VPC & BYOK docs.
transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Maya from Redwood, with Rohit who is our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:00:08] Avery (Ember InfoSec): Good, thanks. We wanted to dig into the security posture — specifically around SOC 2, encryption, and SSO.
[00:00:15] Rohit (Redwood SE): Great, we'll run through our compliance artifacts and deployment options. Quick question up front — are you evaluating hosted first or already leaning toward dedicated/private?
[00:00:26] Dr. Lina (CTO): We're exploring both. For non-PHI workloads hosted might be fine, but for PHI and regulated flows we need stronger guarantees — we're interested in Dedicated or Private with BYOK.
[00:00:36] Samir (Platform): And network isolation. We need VPC peering or an on-prem option.
[00:00:40] Maya: Totally makes sense. Quick overview: Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II report, we also have an ISO 27001 program in progress — I can share the latest artifacts. Hosted comes with our managed control plane; Dedicated gives reserved capacity and stronger tenancy guarantees; Private gives you customer-controlled networking.
[00:01:00] Avery: Can you confirm the SOC 2 coverage — is it for the inference platform, or only control plane? Does it cover encryption at rest?
[00:01:09] Rohit: Our SOC 2 covers both the control plane and data handling for hosted workloads. For Dedicated/Private, the controls shift — we provide the deployment and automation, but the customer has more responsibility depending on the config. Encryption at rest is standard for hosted; keys are managed by our cloud KMS by default.
[00:01:28] Dr. Lina: Our legal/infosec team will want BYOK or HSM integration. Do you support customer-managed KMS?
[00:01:35] Rohit: Yes — we support BYOK via our KMS integration. For Dedicated and Private we can integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and we also support on-prem HSMs for Private deployments. There's a short checklist we use to validate key rotation and access controls.
[00:01:51] Samir: How are audit logs surfaced? We need immutable logs with retention for 7 years for some workflows.
[00:01:58] Maya: We provide detailed audit logs with timestamps, user IDs, and request/response metadata. For Hosted we retain logs per plan; for enterprise we can export logs to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) or S3 for long-term retention.
[00:02:12] Avery: Is the logging tamper-evident? We need chain-of-custody for certain investigations.
[00:02:18] Rohit: We don't presently offer WORM storage natively, but we can export to WORM-enabled S3 buckets on your account when we set up Dedicated/Private. That meets chain-of-custody and long-term retention needs.
[00:02:31] Dr. Lina: SSO is critical. We use SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning. What's the level of support?
[00:02:38] Maya: We support SSO via SAML and OIDC, and SCIM for user provisioning. For RBAC, we have role templates and custom roles in the console.
[00:02:47] Samir: Can roles be mapped to SCIM groups?
[00:02:50] Rohit: Yes — SCIM groups map to RBAC roles. We often see customers map their admin/dev/ops groups and then limit actions like model deployments and key access.
[00:03:00] Avery: We're particularly concerned about who can access inference logs and user prompts. Is there field-level masking or PII redaction?
[00:03:07] Rohit: We provide configurable redaction hooks and support prompt-level filtering. For high-sensitivity flows we recommend routing PHI through a Private deployment with BYOK plus pre-ingest scrubbing.
[00:03:19] Maya: Also, we can configure retention policies per dataset/route — so you can set short retention for ephemeral debug logs and long retention for audit trails.
[00:03:28] [00:03:28] Hana (Procurement): On the procurement side, what controls are in the contract around data ownership and breach notification?
[00:03:34] Maya: We include standard data ownership clauses and a 72-hour breach notification SLA for enterprise plans. We can add specific language for regulated customers as needed.
[00:03:44] Dr. Lina: Latency is also a concern. If we go with Dedicated, can we guarantee p99 latency for our 2k-token flows?
[00:03:52] Rohit: We have SLAs for Dedicated tiers. p95/p99 targets depend on model selection and hardware. For larger context windows we recommend specific instance types. We can run a benchmark using your sample prompts in our staging cluster.
[00:04:05] Samir: Will we be able to do on-prem? We have air-gapped sites for some of our R&D.
[00:04:10] Rohit: Yes. Our Private deployment can be packaged for air-gapped installs. Those are more of a partnership engagement — we provide tooling and deployment automation, but the customer controls the network.
[00:04:19] Avery: For SOC 2, is the Type II report current? What's the scope period?
[00:04:24] Maya: It's current — the report covers Jan-Dec 2025. I'll share the redacted report and a control matrix.
[00:04:30] Dr. Lina: Can you also share the pen test summary?
[00:04:33] Rohit: Yes, we have an annual third-party pentest and quarterly internal scanning. We'll send the executive summary.
[00:04:40] [00:04:40] Avery: What about data residency — some of our customer data must remain in EU. Do you support EU-only hosting?
[00:04:47] Maya: We support region-specific hosting — both Hosted in our EU region and Dedicated pinned to a region. For Private, you can deploy into your EU cloud or on-prem.
[00:04:56] Samir: If we use Hosted but need EU-only retention, can logs and models be pinned?
[00:05:01] Rohit: Models and training assets can be pinned to regions and we can configure log exports to your EU S3. For stricter residency needs we recommend Dedicated with regional tenancy.
[00:05:11] Dr. Lina: Encryption key lifecycle — who has access to the keys? If we do BYOK, can Redwood staff access plaintext?
[00:05:19] Rohit: With BYOK on your KMS account, we never have access to the plaintext keys — Redwood services authenticate to your KMS to decrypt as needed. We can also do HSM-backed flows for higher assurance.
[00:05:31] Avery: Are there SOC controls around privileged access by Redwood staff?
[00:05:35] Maya: Yes, we have least-privilege processes, privileged access reviews, and Just-In-Time access for developers during incident response. All privileged sessions are logged and can be audited.
[00:05:46] Samir: Is there support for customer-managed logging endpoints? We want to push logs to our SIEM, not store them in Redwood.
[00:05:52] Rohit: Absolutely — we support streaming logs to Splunk, Datadog, S3, or a syslog endpoint. It's part of the enterprise integration setup.
[00:05:59] Hana: From procurement perspective re: indemnity and liability — can you point us to standard terms?
[00:06:04] Maya: I'll send the standard enterprise term sheet; we can highlight security addenda and PCI/PHI language where needed.
[00:06:10] [00:06:10] Dr. Lina: Any third-party subprocessors we should be aware of?
[00:06:14] Maya: We list subprocessors in our DPA. They include cloud providers for hosting and a third-party monitoring vendor. We'll provide the current list and any SOC 2 attestations they have.
[00:06:25] Avery: We also need to know about model artifacts — where are model weights stored and how are they protected?
[00:06:31] Rohit: Model artifacts are encrypted at rest. For Hosted they sit in our storage encrypted with our KMS unless BYOK is configured. For Dedicated/Private, you can control the storage account and keys.
[00:06:42] Samir: If we run inference that pulls in PHI, does Redwood persist prompts/outputs by default?
[00:06:48] Maya: By default some telemetry is retained for debugging and quality. For regulated customers we can disable retention or route logs to your account, and also turn on redaction. We'll tailor retention to your policy.
[00:06:59] Dr. Lina: Does Redwood support data deletion requests and can you demonstrate deletion proof for audit?
[00:07:05] Rohit: Yes — we have deletion APIs and can provide an audit trail showing deletion events. For longer retention archives we help coordinate removal from exported stores.
[00:07:15] Maya: Ok want to talk about SSO mapping and RBAC specifics — common patterns we've seen and pitfalls?
[00:07:21] Rohit: Sure. One pitfall is overly broad admin groups. We recommend separate deployer and operator roles, with deployer ability to push model versions but not access logs. Also we support session-based MFA enforcement via SAML.
[00:07:36] Avery: We need approval workflows for model rollouts. Can you block model promotion without an approval step?
[00:07:41] Rohit: Yes — our console supports canary rollouts and approval gates; you can require an approval group before a model becomes default.
[00:07:49] Samir: For Dedicated pricing — is the dedicated pool single-tenant physically, or shared within a tenancy?
[00:07:55] Maya: Dedicated is tenant-isolated capacity — you're not sharing GPUs with other customers. There's also an option for pinned instances if you need stricter isolation.
[00:08:05] Hana: Onboarding timeline — how long to spin up Dedicated or Private?
[00:08:09] Rohit: Dedicated typically 2–4 weeks for standard configs. Private air-gapped installs can be 6–10 weeks depending on approvals and networking.
[00:08:18] Dr. Lina: For the benchmark, can you run our 2k-token prompts with our sample dataset and show p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens?
[00:08:26] Rohit: Yep — we'll need samples and access to a non-production set. We'll run both hosted and dedicated configs and share a spreadsheet.
[00:08:34] Maya: I'll follow up with the SOC2, pentest summary, and the standard enterprise terms. Rohit will send the VPC and BYOK checklist and proposed dates for the technical deep dive.
[00:08:44] Avery: Sounds good. A couple of clarifying points — can you confirm default retention for hosted logs and prompt storage?
[00:08:50] Rohit: Default is 90 days of telemetry for hosted, but enterprise plans allow custom retention and export. Prompts can be configured to not persist at all.
[00:08:59] Samir: Also, can we get references for a couple of healthcare customers who went dedicated?
[00:09:04] Maya: Yes, we can provide references — I'll coordinate with CSM.
[00:09:10] Hana: Any blockers from procurement today? We want to see the term sheet and security pack.
[00:09:15] Maya: We'll send both today.
[00:09:18] [00:09:18] Dr. Lina: Great, thanks.
[00:09:20] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll recap next steps in email.
[00:09:25] Avery: Thanks.
[00:09:27] [END OF CALL]
